orig_commit_message:
fix: fix type of batchOperationKey in camunda-client API to String (#32378)

## Description

The Camunda Client API for batch operations has inconsistent typing for
the batchOperationKey (long and String). This PR changes all remaining
code locations to String.

## Related issues

closes #32205

orig_commit_message:
[CPT] feat: Connect to remote runtime (#32495)

## Description

Introduce a new runtime mode to run the tests on a remote runtime
instead of the Testcontainers runtime from CPT.

- New configuration:
    - `RuntimeMode`: `MANAGED` | `REMOTE`
    - Remote Camunda Monitoring API for purge and clock APIs
    - Remote Connectors API for Inbound connector invocation
- Remote client builder to connect the internal client to the remote
runtime
- Default configuration works for c8run (8.8.0-alpha4)
- CPT checks the connection to the remote runtime on startup

### Connect to local c8run

```
@SpringBootTest(
    classes = {CamundaSpringProcessTestListenerIT.class},
    properties = {"io.camunda.process.test.runtime-mode=remote"})
@CamundaSpringProcessTest
```

### Connect to SaaS

```
@SpringBootTest(
    classes = {CamundaSpringProcessTestListenerIT.class},
    properties = {
  "io.camunda.process.test.runtime-mode=remote",
  "io.camunda.process.test.remote.client.mode=saas",
  "io.camunda.process.test.remote.client.cloud.cluster-id=MY_CLUSTER",
  "io.camunda.process.test.remote.client.cloud.region=syd-1",
  "io.camunda.process.test.remote.client.auth.client-id=MY_CLIENT_ID",
  "io.camunda.process.test.remote.client.auth.client-secret=MY_CLIENT_SECRET",
  "io.camunda.process.test.remote.client.rest-address=https://syd-1.zeebe.camunda.io:443/MY_CLUSTER"
})
@CamundaSpringProcessTest
```

We need to configure the REST address to work around a bug in the client
builder.

## Related issues

closes #25708

Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky

closes #32575

feat: support advanced filter for batch operations (#32764)

## Description

Use advanced operations for all batch operation (item) filter fields.
Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky
and requires some more code.

## Related issues

closes #32575

orig_commit_message:
feat: support advanced filter for batch operations (#32764)

## Description

Use advanced operations for all batch operation (item) filter fields.
Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky
and requires some more code.

## Related issues

closes #32575

Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky
and requires some more code.

## Related issues

closes #32575

orig_commit_message:
feat: support advanced filter for batch operations (#32764)

## Description

Use advanced operations for all batch operation (item) filter fields.
Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky
and requires some more code.

## Related issues

closes #32575

orig_commit_message:
feat: support advanced filter for batch operations (#32764)

## Description

Use advanced operations for all batch operation (item) filter fields.
Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky
and requires some more code.

## Related issues

closes #32575

orig_commit_message:
feat: support advanced filter for batch operations (#32764)

## Description

Use advanced operations for all batch operation (item) filter fields.
Especially to use advanced operations on enums is a little bit tricky
and requires some more code.

## Related issues

closes #32575

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

## Checklist

checked by reviewer. -->

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
refactor: Replace `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with `AsyncRequest` (#32687)

## Description

This PR replaces `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` with a
dedicated `AsyncRequest` model, implemented via new
`AsyncRequestRecord`, `RECEIVED/PROCESSED` events and
`AsyncRequestState`.

### Motivation

Previously, we relied on `UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata` to
associate incoming user task commands (e.g., ASSIGN, UPDATE, COMPLETE)
with their async processing paths. However, this mechanism was:
* tightly coupled to user task operations
* not well-integrated into the record stream
* inflexible to extend for other async-triggered operations (e.g.,
process instance cancelation)

The new `AsyncRequest` mechanism addresses these limitations by
introducing a generic, stream-based model for tracking lifecycle of
deferrable (async) user-triggered commands.

### Key improvements:
* ✅ Introduces `AsyncRequestRecord` with `RECEIVED` and `PROCESSED`
intents
* ✅ Unified handling of async transitions across all user triggered user
task commands and variable updates
* ✅ Improved observability: async flows now emit dedicated events
visible in the record stream
* ✅ Cleanup of legacy metadata storage
(`UserTaskTransitionTriggerRequestMetadata`)
* ✅ Adds test utility method
`assertUserTaskTransitionRelatedIntentsSequence(...)` for asserting
mixed intent flows (`UserTask`, `AsyncRequest`, `VariableDocument`)
* ✅ Enhances test coverage

### Affected transitions:
The following user task operations now emit `AsyncRequest:RECEIVED` and
`AsyncRequest:PROCESSED`:
* `UserTask:ASSIGN`
* `UserTask:CLAIM`
* `UserTask:UPDATE`
* `UserTask:COMPLETE`
* `VariableDocument:UPDATE` (scoped to user task element)

### Follow-ups:
This refactoring enables fixing the following bugs:
* #30686
* #31701
* #33024

orig_commit_message:
The identity migration fails fast on unhandled errors (#33698)

## Description

This change primarily converts the identity migration app to a
CommandLineRunner implementation that runs the migration synchronously
and converts any exception thrown to an exit code = 1. Endless retry
loops from the Identity migration were removed.

In the course of improving the log messages former MigrationRunner
classes for the process and identity migration got renamed to be unique
and the migrator interface extended to provide a name for the migrator.
(Just used the classname now)

The identity migration app is extended with additional log messages on
the cause.

As the identity migration depends on having joined the cluster
successfully the application now busily awaits an initialized topology
state, the interval and max attempts of that are configurable throug the
`camunda.migration.identity.cluster.*` property path and default to a 1s
interval with at max 30 attempts.

orig_commit_message:
feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

orig_commit_message:
feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

orig_commit_message:
feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

orig_commit_message:
feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

orig_commit_message:
feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

orig_commit_message:
feat: use operations for incident search (#33632)

## Description

Uses operations in incident filters in the search layer. This allows
defining specific operations instead of equality only. With this, for
process instance incident search, the tree path matching can be defined
for all data layers at once.

Note: this is a nice preparation for adding advanced search to this
endpoint later as well since all fields support operations then already.

orig_commit_message:
fix: Allow retrying `ADD_VARIABLE` operation with the same variable name (#33928)

> [!TIP]
> For clarity, this PR was intentionally split into focused commits
(improving tests, fix, and small refactoring).
Reviewing it commit-by-commit (rather than as one diff) will make it
easier to understand the purpose and motivation of each change.

## Description

This PR fixes an issue related to `ADD_VARIABLE` operation request
validation that prevented users from retrying a variable addition after
a previous attempt had failed, even though the variable was never
created.

### Motivation

When a variable addition via Operate UI or REST API failed, the
validator would still block any subsequent `ADD_VARIABLE` request with
the same name—even though no variable was actually created.

While this was a rare case before, the introduction of "updating" task
listeners that can dynamically deny user task transitions (e.g., based
on variable value validation logic) makes this a realistic and common
scenario.
In such cases, users should be able to fix the value and trigger
`ADD_VARIABLE` operation with same name.

### Fix
- Changed the check to exclude operations in the `FAILED` state.
- Added a dedicated unit test to confirm that a failed prior operation
does not cause validation failure.

### Refactoring
- Extracted inline validation conditions into helper methods to improve
the readability of `validate(...)` method.

### Test improvements
1. Parameterized missing‐field tests:
- Consolidated many null/empty‐parameter test methods for both
`ADD_VARIABLE` and `UPDATE_VARIABLE` into a single
`@MethodSource`‐driven parameterized test.
2. Parameterized happy‐path tests:
- Replaced two separate “valid request” tests with a single
`@EnumSource({ADD_VARIABLE, UPDATE_VARIABLE})` test.
3. Added missing tests for `"Variable with the name already exists"`
checks.
